sed -i 's/^const ATTRIBUTE_NAMES/\/\/\/ Upper bound of a visibility timeout, in seconds, wherever one is given.\npub const MAX_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT: u64 = 43_200;\n\/\/\/ Upper bound of a delivery delay, in seconds, wherever one is given.\npub const MAX_DELAY_SECONDS: u64 = 900;\n\nconst ATTRIBUTE_NAMES/; s/0\.\.=43_200/0..=MAX_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT/; s/0\.\.=900/0..=MAX_DELAY_SECONDS/' src/attributes.rs
sed -i 's/0\.\.=43_200/0..=MAX_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT/; s/0\.\.=900/0..=MAX_DELAY_SECONDS/; s/^use crate::error::{Error, ErrorCode, Result};/use crate::attributes::{MAX_DELAY_SECONDS, MAX_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT};\nuse crate::error::{Error, ErrorCode, Result};/' src/broker/message_commands.rs
cargo fmt && cargo test 2>&1 | grep -E "test result|error" ; git diff --stat
git commit -qam "Name the visibility timeout and delay limits

The 43_200 and 900 bounds were written out in the attribute parser and
again in the send, receive and change-visibility handlers, so a change to
one could silently leave the others behind. One constant each keeps them
in step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"

input.command:
git add src/queue.rs && git commit -qm "Declare the expiry predicate after the early return

The closure was built on every call, including the common one where
nothing can have expired yet. Moving it below the guard keeps the fast
path to a single comparison.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git commit -qam "Stop ignoring a missing message in ChangeMessageVisibility

in_flight_message has just resolved the handle to a live message, so the
lookup cannot fail. The silent if-let would have hidden a broken
invariant as a successful no-op; expect names the invariant instead.
